correctness.rationale: For every n≥0 the two shifts reduce common roots to remainders of degrees one and two. At d=2 Stern adjacent coprimality plus monicity forces s(n+2)=1, hence n+2=2^h; the only candidate rational root has modulus h+1 while all P_{2^h-2} roots have modulus at most h, with n=0 handled separately. At d=3 even n the quadratic remainder factors over R, whereas P_even is everywhere positive by an explicitly proved recurrence identity. Odd n gives an irreducible primitive quadratic with leading coefficient u+v>1, which cannot divide a monic integer P_n by Gauss lemma. The Stern identities and positive-coefficient root bound are proved or explicitly supplied; symbolic computations for n≤81 and standalone modular gcd checks for n<128 validate indexing only, not infinity.

value.rationale: The 2021 introduction of coefficient-Stern polynomials singles out resultant and factor questions and proves precisely the adjacent case. The first two nonadjacent separations are natural structural tests of whether the family has common complex roots, rather than arbitrary finite parameters or a table recomputation. The combined all-index theorem identifies two different mechanisms—arithmetic size of a forced rational root and integral primitivity of an irreducible quadratic—that apply uniformly despite wild Stern coefficients. It is a meaningful partial resolution of the explicit adjacent-to-general-pairs gap, without claiming a general all-offset theorem or a closed resultant formula.
